---
title: "Generative Adversarial Networks"
---

### What is a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) and what is it used for? 

A GAN is a machine learning model used to generate unique images. It is called an "*adversarial*" network because there are two pieces fighting against each other to create the best outcome. 

The two models working inside a GAN are the [*Generator*](#generator) and the [*Discriminator*](#discriminator). These two pieces challenge each other, trying to catch the other in an error, which makes each program better in the end. 

> Throughout this blog you will see examples from code written with the help of an AI model (Claude by Anthropic). This is to help visualize and understand what is going on inside the GAN 


### The Generator {#generator}

In a GAN,  the *Generator's* job is to produce unique images. The problem the Generator faces is knowing *what* to come up with when creating these unique images. The first time the Generator runs it, has no data to work with, so it just comes up with nonsense. See Fig1 

![**Fig1:** A GAN Generator's first attempt at making an image](images/epoch_00001.png)

This initial output (a bunch of visual noise) isn't what we want. In order to get a more useful output we need to teach the Generator that this output is not what we want. This is where the Discriminator comes in. 


### The Discriminator {#discriminator}

The Discriminator compares the generated images with real images from a training dataset. In this example our dataset consists of small pixelmaps of 5-point stars, see Fig2. 

::: {layout-ncol=5}

![**Fig2-a**](images/star_0.png)

![**Fig2-b**](images/star_1.png)

![**Fig2-c**](images/star_2.png)

![**Fig2-d**](images/star_3.png)

![**Fig2-e**](images/star_4.png)

:::

The Discriminator looks at the real dataset, and the generated images and tries to determine whether a given image is fake (from the Generator) or real (from the dataset). 


### Two Real World Examples

#### A Real (Fake) Example of a Generator and Discriminator

> A Counterfeiter is trying to make fake money, and the Police are trying to catch him. It's a game of cops and robbers. The Counterfeiter makes their first $1 bill and uses it at a store. The Police find the bill and compare it to a *real* $1 bill to determine the one from the store is a fake. The Counterfeiter is caught! 
> 
> The Counterfeiter looks at the failed fake and tries again, changing some of the pieces of the $1 bill to make it look more realistic. He brings this $1 bill back to the store and tries to use it. When the bill is intercepted by the Police they check it against what they know as real money. This time, the fake bill looks so real that the Police can't tell the difference! The counterfeit bill never gets caught. 

#### A Real (Real) Example of an Adversarial Network

> This technique of an adversarial network is also a common approach for solving real security issues. In Cyber Security it is common to have a team, the Good Guys and a team, the Bad Guys. The Good Guys try to create security protocols that prevent malicious users from getting into a network, protecting user and company data/resources. 
>
> But how do you know if the security measures are good? The Bad Guys go in and try to break down all the work the Good Guys did. This allows for companies to find problems in security in a safe and manageable way, instead of allowing *real* bad guys (hackers and other criminals) to find the weak spots first. 

Generator | Discriminator | Adversarial Network
---|---|---
A Counterfeiter Creating Fake Money | The Police Investigating the Money | Ongoing Battle Between Counterfeiters and Police 
Bad Guys | Good Guys | Cyber Security Defense Teams  

### Putting it Together

In a GAN system the [Discriminator](#discriminator) is fed both real *and* fake images. Each time the Discriminator is learning how to tell them apart. Whenever a Discriminator correctly predicts an image, it gets positive feedback; each time it's wrong the Discriminator gets negative feedback. This process of getting feedback is called ***backpropagation***.

The [Generator](#generator) is also receiving immediate feedback on whether it passed the Discriminator or not. If the Discriminator fails, the Generator wins. If the Discriminator succeeds the Generator loses. Each win and loss tells the Generator if it's doing a good job creating the image. 

**The Math**

The mathematic definition of this competition can express as follows: 

$$
\min_G \max_D V(D,G)
=
\mathbb{E}_{x\sim p_{\text{data}}}[\log D(x)]
+
\mathbb{E}_{z\sim p_z}[\log(1-D(G(z)))]
$$
This is a standard GAN equation where $G$ preresents the Generator and $D$ represents the Discriminator. The Generator takes random noise $z$ and producs and image $G(z)$, while the Discriminator estimates whether an image is real.

The Discriminator tries to maximize this objective by correctly identifying real images, while the Generator tries to minimize it by producing images that fool the Discriminator.

This system loops through thousands of times generating and discriminating images over and over again until the final Generator consistently beats the Discriminator. 

We call these loops ***epochs*** and we can see the progress throughout the epochs in the figures below. 

::: {layout-ncol=3}

![Epoch 1000](images/epoch_01000.png)

![Epoch 1500](images/epoch_01500.png)

![Epoch 2000](images/epoch_02000.png)

![Epoch 2500](images/epoch_02500.png)

![Epoch 3000](images/epoch_03000.png)

![Epoch 3500](images/epoch_03500.png)

![Epoch 4000](images/epoch_04000.png)

![Epoch 4500](images/epoch_04500.png)

![Epoch 5000](images/epoch_05000.png)

As the epochs progress the images get more and more clear, and actually start to look like the training dataset. 


### Try it yourself

Here is all the code used to build and train a Generator and Discriminator for a GAN. Enjoy! 

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Necessary Imports, Macros and Helper Functions"
import math
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from PIL import Image

IMG_SIZE = 16          # images are IMG_SIZE x IMG_SIZE
RADIUS = 2.5           # circle radius
NOISE_DIM = 32
N_REAL_SAMPLES = 2000  # how many synthetic "real" images to generate
EPOCHS = 5000
SHAPE = "star"         # "star" or "circle"

DATA_SEED = 0                  # fixed, so the dataset is identical every render
TRAIN_SEED = int(time.time())  # set to a fixed int for reproducible training
torch.manual_seed(TRAIN_SEED)

# All paths are relative to the folder the .qmd / script lives in
ROOT = Path(".")
DATA_DIR = ROOT / "data"
SAMPLE_DIR = ROOT / "samples"
SNAPSHOT_DIR = ROOT / "snapshots"
G_PATH = ROOT / f"{SHAPE}_generator.pt"

def load_dataset(name, n, data_seed=DATA_SEED):
    """Load a cached dataset if it exists, otherwise generate and save it.
    Stored as bool (images are binary) to keep the file small.
    """
    path = DATA_DIR / f"{name}_n{n}_seed{data_seed}.pt"
    mask = torch.load(path)

    return mask.float() * 2 - 1  # back to [-1, 1]

def to_uint8(imgs):
    """(-1,1) tensor -> uint8 numpy array in [0, 255]."""
    return ((imgs.detach().cpu().numpy() + 1) / 2 * 255).astype("uint8")

def save_samples(n=5):
    """Save a few real training images as individual PNGs."""
    for i, img in enumerate(to_uint8(REAL_DATA[:n])):
        Image.fromarray(img).resize((128, 128), Image.NEAREST).save(
            SAMPLE_DIR / f"{SHAPE}_{i}.png"
        )

def save_grid(imgs, path, nrow=5, pad=2, scale=8):
    """Save a batch of (-1,1)-range images as one PNG grid."""
    imgs = to_uint8(imgs)
    n = imgs.shape[0]
    nrows_grid = -(-n // nrow)  # ceil
    cell = IMG_SIZE + pad
    grid = np.zeros((nrows_grid * cell, nrow * cell), dtype="uint8")
    for i, im in enumerate(imgs):
        r, c = divmod(i, nrow)
        grid[r * cell: r * cell + IMG_SIZE, c * cell: c * cell + IMG_SIZE] = im
    Image.fromarray(grid).resize(
        (grid.shape[1] * scale, grid.shape[0] * scale), Image.NEAREST
    ).save(path)

REAL_DATA = load_dataset(SHAPE, N_REAL_SAMPLES)  # (N, IMG_SIZE, IMG_SIZE)

```

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Class Definitions (Generator and Discriminator)"

class Generator(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(NOISE_DIM, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, IMG_SIZE * IMG_SIZE),
            nn.Tanh(),  # output in [-1, 1], same range as the real data
        )

    def forward(self, z):
        return self.net(z).view(-1, IMG_SIZE, IMG_SIZE)


class Discriminator(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(IMG_SIZE * IMG_SIZE, 128),
            nn.LeakyReLU(0.2),
            nn.Linear(128, 128),
            nn.LeakyReLU(0.2),
            nn.Linear(128, 1),  # raw logit
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x.view(x.size(0), -1))
```

```{python}
save_samples() # Saves 5 images from the load_dataset
batch_size = 64
lr=2e-4
print_every = 500
snapshot_dir = Path(SNAPSHOT_DIR)

# Creating two Generator and Discriminator objects
G, D = Generator(), Discriminator() 
opt_g = torch.optim.Adam(G.parameters(), lr=lr, betas = (0.5, 0.999))
opt_d = torch.optim.Adam(D.parameters(), lr=lr, betas=(0.5, 0.999))
loss_fn = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()
fixed_z = torch.randn(20, NOISE_DIM) # same noise for each snapshot, so we can watch it evolve

# Looping throught the predetermined number of EPOCHS
for epoch in range(1, EPOCHS + 1):
    # Getting a random sample from the real image dataset
    idx = torch.randint(0, len(REAL_DATA), (batch_size,))
    real = REAL_DATA[idx]

    # Generating an image with the generator
    z = torch.randn(batch_size, NOISE_DIM)
    fake = G(z)

    # === Train Discriminator ===
    opt_d.zero_grad()
    real_pred = D(real)
    fake_pred = D(fake.detach())
    d_loss = loss_fn(real_pred, torch.full_like(real_pred, 0.9)) + \
        loss_fn(fake_pred, torch.zeros_like(fake_pred))
    d_loss.backward()
    opt_d.step()

    # === Train Generator ===
    opt_g.zero_grad()
    fake_pred = D(fake)
    g_loss = loss_fn(fake_pred, torch.ones_like(fake_pred))
    g_loss.backward()
    opt_g.step()

    if epoch % print_every == 0 or epoch == 1:
        print(f"epoch {epoch:5d} | D loss {d_loss.item():.3f} | G loss {g_loss.item():.3f}")
        with torch.no_grad():
            samples = G(fixed_z)
        save_grid(samples, snapshot_dir / f"epoch_{epoch:05d}.png")
    
torch.save(G.state_dict(), G_PATH)

with torch.no_grad():
    save_grid(G(torch.randn(20, NOISE_DIM)), ROOT / f"{SHAPE}_final.png")

```
